Messages.Author: _angst_
Messages.Body:
Hi
We had some "misunderstandings" in our last tourney. And I wonder how
you would have judged them. And I also wonder what "official" sources
(LSJ) would have done.
My ruling in both cases was issuing a warning for the player in error.
A majority of the players didn't want to see any disqualifications at
the event.

Here are the different scenarios:

1.) A players uses a sabbat vampire to play Justicar Retribution
burning his/hers predators Francois Villon (that had heart of the city
or something similar on him, can't remember exactly). The error was not
noticed by any of the five players at the tabel. When the error was
realised the game was almost over and it was to late to backtrack.

2.) A player realises that he/she is playing with a eleven card crypt.
The player in question played a borrowed deck.

What would you have done in one of your local tourneys?
What would you have done if the occured in a big qualifier or similar
event?

Best wishes
Alex Ek
Prince of Gothenburg

Messages.Author: Emmit Svenson
Messages.Body:
_angst_ wrote:
> 1.) A players uses a sabbat vampire to play Justicar Retribution
> burning his/hers predators Francois Villon (that had heart of the city
> or something similar on him, can't remember exactly). The error was not
> noticed by any of the five players at the tabel. When the error was
> realised the game was almost over and it was to late to backtrack.

I'd issue a warning to the player if I thought he made a mistake or a
game loss if I thought it was deliberate. Either way, I'd give his
predator his Francois Villon back, untapped, with all the cards that
were on him and full of blood.

Tough one for the judge. It's a problem so greivous there's no real way
to fix it to everyone's satisfaction.

> 2.) A player realises that he/she is playing with a eleven card crypt.
> The player in question played a borrowed deck.

I'd issue a caution, move a random one of his uncontrolled vampires to
his crypt and replace it in his uncontrolled region with a duplicate of
one of his ready vampires.

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
_angst_ wrote:
>
> He controlled no camarilla vampire to play the card.
> One of the biggest problems with backtracking this was that when the
> error was realised Francois controller was already ousted
> Luckily for me there was no fighting over this problem. The predator in
> question was abit annoyed but thought it would be best for the game not
> to try to backtrack. I just want to know some guidelines if I face this
> problem again.
>

Well, you know, it's everybody's responsibility to make sure that
vampires playing cards meet the requirements. If the player who played
it made a mistake, the player affected should have noticed it, or
possibly the other people at the table. Obviously, that doesn't always
happen, mistakes are made, and if it was possible to rewind, then you
should rewind. But if it's not possible, the player who lost his
Francois can't really be any more annoyed at the guy who played the JR
than he should be at himself for not catching it at the time.

ahem ... I did it one time. Playing in a final, burning Leandro of my
predator with an Justicar Retribution from Gratiano. I had not read the
card text right. Nobody noticed it until a week later.

What can you do? It is like in soccer, when the camera shows afterwards
that the ball was not in the goal.

And in the game you also cannot rewind everything. So you have to apply
what seems apropriate. If it was his prey that afterwards got ousted,
let him lose the 6 pool. If he would never have ousted his prey, let
him lose the VP. Like Johannes said, you could give the VP to the
ousted player. You have to judge, what could have happened and what is
appropriate to rebalance the situation. But that can never be perfect.
But it will be better to let the game go on, than to screw it complete
because of a mistake done at the beginning.
